title: Theory Test Day Checklist
summary: What to bring, how both parts of the lorry theory test work and what happens after.

blocks.text: The Driver CPC part 1 theory test has two parts: multiple choice and hazard perception. You book them separately, but you can take them on the same day, in either order.

blocks.title: Bring with you
items: A Great Britain photocard driving licence, or
A Northern Ireland photocard licence and paper counterpart, or
An EU photocard licence (and paper counterpart, if you have one).
Paper licence only? Bring a valid passport too.
Changed your name since booking? Bring proof, like a marriage certificate or deed poll.

blocks.title: No documents, no test
blocks.text: If you don't bring the right documents, your test is cancelled and you lose your fee.

blocks.title: The days before
items: Book through the official GOV.UK service: £26 for multiple choice and £11 for hazard perception.
Questions are based on The Highway Code, Know Your Traffic Signs and the DVSA guide to driving goods vehicles.
Read the traps on your maps one last time, especially drivers' hours and loads.
Practise hazard perception with the official DVSA guide to hazard perception.

blocks.title: Multiple choice
items: You get instructions and a practice question first.
You can flag questions and come back to them.
You can review and change any answer before you finish.
You don't have to use the full 1 hour 55 minutes.

blocks.title: Hazard perception
items: 19 clips; each has at least one developing hazard, and one clip has two.
Up to 5 points for each developing hazard: click as soon as it starts to develop.
Clicking continuously or in a pattern scores nothing.
One attempt per clip: you can't review or change responses.

blocks.title: After the test
items: You get a results letter at the test centre for each part.
Pass both parts within 2 years of each other to get your theory test certificate.
The certificate is valid for 2 years from passing the first part: pass parts 3a and 3b within that time.
Failed? You can book again straight away, but you can't take the test for 3 clear working days.
